items.title: Japan agrees to buy up to 8 mln barrels of Saudi crude to rebuild oil reserves
items.summary: ISTANBUL: Japan has agreed to buy up to 8 million barrels of Saudi crude for its national petroleum reserve if market conditions are favourable, the two countries said Friday, Anadolu Ajansi reported, citing Saudi Press Agency. The agreement also expands the storage capacity available to Saudi Arabia in Japan. Saudi Arabia has already begun replenishing crude stocks at storage facilities in Japan, the statement said.

items.title: News@9 – Friday, November 20, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Ismail Lasim to continue as Negri MB Datuk Ismail Lasim will remain as Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar after Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir consented to retain him in the post. Flood concern Rapid hill-clearing and slope-stabilisation works are underway near settlements in Bukit Cherakah, Jeram, Ijok, Puncak Alam and Bukit Kapar, raising concerns over worsening flash floods. Chan Sow Lin scrapyard fire A car scrapyard in Jalan Utusan, off Jalan Chan Sow Lin, was 90 per cent destroyed in a fire early today.

items.title: 'Every year my house floods': Rantau Panjang braces for rising waters
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Residents in Rantau Panjang are keeping a close watch on Sungai Golok as its rising water level fuels fears of flooding, particularly if rain continues. Resident Nik Ahmad Nik Ismail, 40, said the rising water level had prompted him to check the river more frequently. Another resident, Wan Che Zainab Wan Che Mat, 55, said heavy rain in Narathiwat had heightened anxiety among those living near the river.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Friday, Nov 20, 2026
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. items.title: ITMAX to raise RM1bil from sukuk issuances
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: ITMAX System Bhd has established two Islamic financing programmes with a combined limit of RM1 billion to fund its business operations and refinance existing borrowings. The smart city solutions provider said its wholly owned ITMAX Capital Sdn Bhd lodged the required documents with the Securities Commission for an Islamic medium-term notes (IMTN) programme and an Islamic commercial papers (ICP) programme. AmInvestment Bank Bhd is the principal adviser, lead arranger, lead manager, facility agent and security agent, while AmBank Islamic Bhd is the Islamic adviser.

items.title: Three held as police uncover RM1.27mil stash of health and beauty products
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police detained three men and seized health, cosmetic and food products worth RM1.27 million in a raid on a logistics premises in Banting, Selangor, yesterday. Checks uncovered 1,044 boxes of health and cosmetic products, 1,300 bottles of supplements and health products, 38 boxes of tremella soup products, 65 boxes of coenzyme Q10 products, as well as various tea-based food and beverage products and snacks. The Kuala Langat District Health Office seized items worth RM5,167, while the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry accounted for RM4,745.

items.title: Firefighters save woman threatening to jump into sea
items.summary: LANGKAWI: Firefighters rescued a 35-year-old woman who threatened to jump into the sea from a breakwater at Kuala Muda here today. Kedah Zone 4 Fire and Rescue Department chief Mohd Zamri Abdul Ghani said seven firefighters from the Padang Mat Sirat Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the scene after receiving an emergency call at 3.16pm. Zamri said firefighters approached the woman and managed to persuade her to move to safety.

items.title: Evidence in former Petronas manager's case met international standards, court told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Evidence stored by CyberSecurity Malaysia in the case involving former Petronas manager Mohd Khairul Akmal fully complied with international standards set by the American Society of Crime Laboratory Directors (ASCLD), the Sessions Court heard today. CyberSecurity Malaysia Senior Digital Forensic Analyst Abdul Wafi Abdul Rahman, 38, said the agency's internal chain-of-custody procedures applied only within its forensic laboratory. The seventh prosecution witness was responding to questions during re-examination by Deputy Public Prosecutor Noor Syafina Mohd Radzuan in the trial of Mohd Khairul Akmal, who is charged with attempting to disclose Petronas' business report and financial structure to Petroleum Sarawak Bhd (Petros) on June 8, 2024.

items.title: 'They were inseparable': Siblings, 13 and 10, die in house fire [WATCH]
items.summary: TAWAU: "Muhammad Nor Fazryn always looked after his younger sister, wherever he went. Noreen said her nephew, Muhammad Nor Fazryn Norman, and his 10-year-old sister, Nurailin Nathania, who was autistic, were trapped in an upstairs room of their double-storey terrace house when the fire broke out about 6am. The room's windows were fitted with security grilles, leaving the children with no way out, she said.

items.title: MN Holdings lands record RM1.12bil solar deal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MN Holdings Bhd has secured its biggest contract to date, a RM1.12 billion deal as part of a consortium to build two large-scale solar farms in Kemaman, Terengganu. The engineering and construction contract also marks the group's first entry into the large-scale solar segment. The project was awarded by RE Kemaman Sdn Bhd and RE Kemaman II Sdn Bhd under the LSS Petra 5+ programme.

items.title: Flood victims told to register or risk missing out on aid
items.summary: KUALA SELANGOR: Flood victims have been advised to register with the authorities immediately, whether they are staying at temporary relief centres or in their own homes, to ensure they do not miss out on assistance. Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said registration was crucial to ensure victims' details were recorded and aid could be distributed efficiently. Also present were Selangor Social Welfare Department director Azmir Kassim and Kuala Selangor district officer Mohd Raiz Radzuan.

items.title: Sabah PH eyes more seats, but 3 remain non-negotiable
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Sabah Pakatan Harapan (PH) will defend the three parliamentary seats it currently holds while exploring opportunities to contest additional seats in the 16th General Election (GE16). Its chairman, Datuk Mustapha Sakmud, said the three seats were Sepanggar, which he represents, and Kota Kinabalu and Sandakan, currently held by DAP representatives. Also present were Sabah Amanah chairman Datuk Lahirul Latigu, Sabah DAP deputy chairman Datuk Chan Foong Hin and Sabah PH secretary Datuk Ruji Ubi.

items.title: 'He kept his promise to care for mum until their final day'
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: "My younger brother once promised us he would look after our mother. His mother, Jamilah Bebe Abd Rahman, 63, and brother, Abdul Rahim Abdul Muthaliff, 36, were found burnt to death in their respective bedrooms. "He called me and said, 'Hafiz, be strong.

items.title: Moody's affirms Affin's A3 rating
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Moody's Ratings has reaffirmed Affin Group's long-term credit rating at A3 with a stable outlook, citing its sound financial fundamentals, good asset quality and support from Sarawak. "Moody's expects Affin Group to maintain healthy asset quality, with its tangible common equity to risk-weighted assets ratio remaining in the 14 per cent to 15 per cent range in 2027. Affin Group president and group chief executive officer Datuk Wan Razly Abdullah said the reaffirmation reflected confidence in the group's long-term growth prospects.

items.title: Negri MB shuts door on bid to remove Tuanku Muhriz
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has declared the April 19 proclamation seeking to remove Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the state's ruler invalid, saying it will not be gazetted. The proclamation , issued amid a dispute involving the state's traditional ruling chiefs, or Undang, sought to depose Tuanku Muhriz and replace him with Tuanku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja'afar. Also present at the palace were Undang Luak Rembau Datuk Hassan Ab Hamid, Undang Luak Sungai Ujong Datuk Muhammad Faris Johari and Undang Luak Jelebu Datuk Azrin Khairi.

items.title: Wawasan Dengkil's Q1 profit slips 23pct
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Wawasan Dengkil Holdings Bhd's net profit fell 23.33 per cent to RM2.07 million in the first quarter (Q1) ended September 30, 2026 compared to RM2.70 million a year earlier due to higher administrative expenses. In its filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said its revenue rose 11.28 per cent to RM59.18 million in Q1 2026 compared to RM53.18 million last year. Barring any unforeseen circumstances, Wawasan Dengkil said it remains cautiously optimistic of its prospects for the coming financial year.

items.title: 'No time, I'm in a rush': Jalaluddin sidesteps MB controversy
items.summary: JELEBU: Negri Sembilan Umno liaison committee chairman Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias today declined to comment on the Menteri Besar controversy, saying he was in a hurry. Earlier, Jalaluddin, who is also Pertang assemblyman, had jokingly warned reporters against asking him about Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim. Earlier today, Ismail, 67, who is also Juasseh assemblyman, announced that he would remain as Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar .

items.title: YTL Power denies links to Nvidia GPU allegations
items.summary: Azanis Shahila Aman KUALA LUMPUR: YTL Power International Bhd today denied allegations linking its Johor data centres to the alleged transfer of Nvidia graphics processing units (GPUs) to Chinese customers. YTL Power said its data centre subsidiary YTL Data Centers provides co-location services including space, power, cooling and connectivity to multiple global customers, including US hyperscalers. The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim final rule on Nov 19 to prevent companies in countries of concern, including China, from accessing large volumes of advanced computing power through data centres overseas.

items.title: Selangor bears brunt as 2,372 flood victims remain displaced
items.summary: Selangor continued to record the highest number of evacuees, with 1,786 victims from 489 families housed at 14 centres across four districts. Among the centres, Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Dato' Maharaja Lela was sheltering 394 victims, followed by SK Parit Mahang (365) and Sekolah Rendah Agama Bukit Kuching (236). In Perak, 477 victims from 163 families were housed at seven centres across five districts.

items.title: Seven RMAF personnel held over RM4.83mil drug haul
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Seven Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) personnel, including five officers, have been detained to assist investigations into the discovery of 96.6kg of suspected drugs at Subang Air Base on Tuesday. RMAF chief General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris said the other two detainees were personnel of different ranks. The discovery was made by RMAF personnel at the Air Movement Section (AMS) building at Subang Air Base.

items.title: Aeon's Q3 earnings fall 36pct on higher tax expenses
items.summary: Bursa Malaysia filing showed the retailer's tax expense surged to RM17.30 million from RM4 million, mainly due to higher deferred tax charges, which rose to RM16.70 million from RM1 million. Quarterly revenue rose 1.59 per cent to RM1.01 billion from RM995.20 million, supported by higher contributions from its retail and property management businesses. Despite the decline in net profit, Aeon's operating profit rose 18.12 per cent to RM50.20 million from RM42.50 million, supported by effective cost management and improved operational efficiency.

items.title: SFP Tech's Q3 earnings surge eightfold to RM5.81mil on stronger manufacturing demand
items.summary: The automation segment contributed the remaining RM7.63 million, compared with RM2.97 million previously. For the first nine months, SFP Tech's net profit rose 82.76 per cent to RM15.21 million from RM8.32 million a year ago, while revenue increased 60.46 per cent to RM113.89 million from RM70.98 million. Total liabilities increased to RM129.71 million from RM104.74 million, while borrowings rose to RM67.17 million from RM56.44 million.

items.title: Bangladesh hit by fresh arson attacks amid political unrest
items.summary: DHAKA: Fresh arson attacks erupted in Bangladesh on Friday as authorities restored communications with the hometown of convicted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, following days of unrest over her planned return from exile. Hasina's former ruling party, the Awami League, whose activities are now banned, called for strikes this week to mark the anniversary of the day she received her death sentence. Kobir said Dhaka would deal with attacks "very firmly".

items.title: RHB banks secure top AAA rating
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: RAM Ratings has upgraded the financial institution ratings of RHB Bank Bhd, RHB Islamic Bank Bhd and RHB Investment Bank Bhd to AAA/Stable/P1 from AA1/Positive/P1. RHB today said the upgrade was underpinned by the group's strengthened funding profile, strong capitalisation, healthy asset quality and sustained profitability. Group managing director and group chief executive officer Datuk Mohd Rashid Mohamad said the AAA rating reflected years of disciplined execution, prudent risk management and continued confidence from customers, shareholders and business partners.

items.title: Betel-leaf stall, two sundry shops sealed in Penang crackdown on foreign-run businesses
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Three businesses operating without valid licences were sealed by the Penang Island City Council (MBPP) during an enforcement operation targeting foreign-run premises and licensing violations. At a premises in Jalan Oldham, officers found an unlicensed business selling betel leaves (sirih) and beverages without a valid 2026 council permit. "Three foreigners were found at the premises, including one without valid identification documents.

items.title: 32 transactions, RM85,468 missing: NGO director arrested
items.summary: KANGAR: An NGO director has been arrested at Kuala Lumpur International Airport Terminal 2 (KLIA2) over the alleged misappropriation of RM85,468 in organisational funds. Perlis police chief Deputy Commissioner Hamzah Hashim said the 31-year-old man was detained at the domestic arrival gate at 11.05am today after arriving on a flight from Sabah. He said the arrest followed intelligence gathering and was linked to a criminal breach of trust investigation opened on Nov 13.

items.title: Parking row sparks Cheras brawl; two Chinese citizens arrested after violent clash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A dispute over a parking space erupted into a violent brawl involving several men armed with suspected iron rods outside a convenience store in Taman Connaught, Cheras, early today. Cheras police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Rosdi Daud said police received a report on the fight, which was believed to have stemmed from a misunderstanding over vehicle parking. "Acting on information received, personnel from the Cheras police headquarters' D7 Division arrested two Chinese citizens at Jalan 9, Taman Len Seng, at 5am.

items.title: [UPDATED] RMAF drug trafficking probe: 2 more arrested in Tawau, bringing total to 7
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Two more Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) personnel have been arrested in Tawau, Sabah, bringing the number of air force personnel held in connection with a cross-border drug trafficking syndicate to seven. The latest arrests bring the total number of suspects detained to 13, including six civilians, among them two alleged syndicate coordinators, following operations in the Klang Valley, Labuan and Sabah. "The two who were remanded are the latest arrests made at RMAF Tawau.

items.title: Bank Negara, Philippines' Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas deepen ties in Islamic finance, digital payments
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia and the Philippines' Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen cooperation in several key areas. Bank Negara governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said these include Islamic finance, cross-border payment linkages, local currency transactions, financial innovation and digitalisation. BSP governor Eli M Remolona Jr said the MoU marked another important step in the longstanding partnership between the two central banks.

items.title: 'Bonebridge' implant opens up new world of hearing for Amirul
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A 19-year-old student born without external ears and with congenital hearing loss is experiencing a new lease of life after undergoing a Bonebridge hearing implant procedure at the Canselor Tuanku Muhriz Hospital (HCTM) on Nov 12. Unlike conventional hearing aids, which amplify sound through the ear canal, the Bonebridge system consists of an internal implant and an external audio processor worn over the implant site. For Muhammad Amirul Hakimi Sani, who previously relied on conventional hearing aids, the procedure has improved his ability to hear, boosting his confidence in socialising and keeping up with his studies.

items.title: Taking the ECRL? Here’s what to expect onboard, including one very Malaysian necessity (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 20 — The excitement of taking a new train service is really about the experience and discovering what amenities await. As the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) prepares to connect communities across the east coast when commercial passenger services begin next month, here’s what passengers can expect from the onboard six-car electric train experience. Beyond the swivel seating arrangement, passengers can also choose between two travel classes: Economy and Business, each offering its own level of comfort and amenities.

items.title: Anwar says court scrutiny can override secrecy of Pardons Board documents
items.summary: SHENZHEN (China), Nov 19 — The original documents of the Pardons Board are classified as confidential, but their declassification is not unusual if they are challenged through court proceedings, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said applications or challenges through the courts involving such documents could normally lead to their declassification, while the date of implementation would be determined later. “The original documents are indeed confidential, but usually, if they are brought to court, they are declassified.

items.title: Johor halts Pontian land reclamation over suspected dumping of foreign construction waste
items.summary: PONTIAN, Nov 19 — The Johor state government has ordered an immediate halt to land reclamation works at a project site suspected of using construction waste believed to have originated from a neighbouring country at Jalan Kampung Tenggayun, Mukim Rimba Terjun, here. State Housing and Local Government Committee deputy chairman Zaidi Japar said the order was issued following the detection of various regulatory violations, including carrying out works without approval of Form B from the Pontian Municipal Council (MPPn) president. He said the violations identified at the site, which had been active for the past week, included non-compliance with traffic management requirements, the installation of hoarding and signboards, waste management, and carrying out works without Form B approval.

items.title: Chow Kon Yeow defends Penang’s RM8.4b water deal, says payments cover plant costs over 40 years
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 19 — The RM8.4 billion Capacity Charge payable over 40 years under the Bulk Water Supply Agreement (BWSA) between Penang and Perak represents deferred payments to recover the construction costs of a water treatment plant built specifically to supply water to Penang. It is a standard payment mechanism in long-term bulk water supply agreements and is separate from charges for the actual volume of water supplied, he said. He explained that the water treatment plant, with a capacity of 500 million litres per day (MLD), was constructed exclusively to supply the Penang Water Supply Corporation (PBAPP), at an estimated construction cost of RM3 billion.

items.title: KL prepares 86 classrooms for six-year-olds starting Year One in 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 19 — A total of 86 classrooms at 48 schools in the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur have been prepared to accommodate six-year-old pupils entering Year One from 2027. The ministry said the initiative was expected to benefit 3,820 pupils in three districts, namely Bangsar Pudu (45 schools), Keramat (25 schools) and Sentul (16 schools). Meanwhile, the 2027 Academic Calendar for National Schools and Government-Aided Schools will run from January 4 to December 2, 2027, for schools in Group A states, and from January 4 to December 3, 2027, for those in Group B states.

items.title: Anwar calls for independent probe into Perak boarding school student’s death
items.summary: Anwar said he had discussed the incident with the police and Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, describing it as something he had never imagined could happen. Anwar also questioned the supervision and care provided to students at boarding schools, particularly when students are absent from class or staying in areas such as the sick bay. Boarding schools have designated areas for students requiring care in the sick bay.

items.title: Puchong chicken slaughterhouse to face Syariah, licensing charges next week
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 19 — A premises in Puchong, suspected of operating as a non-Syariah-compliant chicken slaughtering and processing centre, is expected to face charges next week for several offences, including offences under the state’s Syariah enactment. Selangor Islamic Religious Affairs and Cultural Innovation Committee chairman Dr Mohammad Fahmi Ngah said the premises, believed to have operated since 2004, will also face charges under local authority regulations, including licensing offences. Selangor Islamic Religious Council (Mais) chairman Datuk Salehuddin Saidin previously said the premises in Puchong, believed to be a chicken slaughtering, processing and distribution hub operating without a valid halal certificate, was found to use an electric water-bath stunning method in handling the poultry.

items.title: Penang motorists face 221 days of diversions along Jalan Tun Dr Awang for LRT works
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 19 — Traffic diversions in both directions along Jalan Tun Dr Awang in Bayan Lepas will be in place for 221 days from November 21 to facilitate piling works and the construction of permanent structures for the Mutiara Line Light Rail Transit (LRT) project. “The diversions will cover sections of Jalan Tun Dr Awang from Kompleks Sri Relau to Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Cina (SJKC) Min Sin towards Komtar, and between Amari SPICE Hotel and the SPICE Aquatic Centre towards Bayan Lepas. “The diversions are necessary to facilitate preliminary works for the Mutiara Line LRT project, involving piling and permanent structural works,” it said.

items.title: Baby girl found buried behind Pantai Remis home after suspected stabbing, mother and boyfriend held
items.summary: IPOH, Nov 19 — A newborn baby girl, believed to have been stabbed by her biological mother, died in an incident in Pantai Remis on November 14. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the incident is believed to have occurred on the day the baby was born, at about 1pm. He said the initial investigation found that the baby’s mother, who is 19 years old, committed the act at her home before contacting her boyfriend to help bury the baby’s body behind her house.

items.title: Five new faces join Melaka exco as 10 assemblymen sworn in
items.summary: Ab Rauf said the five new appointees were Ayer Molek assemblyman Datuk Mohd Ridhwan Mohd Ali, who will oversee the Education, Higher Education and TVET portfolio; Kelebang assemblyman Datuk Lim Ban Hong (Health and Human Capital); and Gadek assemblyman S. Nadarajah (Youth, Sports and NGOs). Ab Rauf said the five executive councillors retained were Merlimau assemblyman Datuk Dr Muhammad Akmal Saleh (Science, Technology, Innovation and Digital Communications); Sungai Udang assemblyman Datuk Rais Yasin (Religion, Entrepreneur Development, Cooperatives and Cost of Living); and Telok Mas assemblyman Datuk Abdul Razak Abdul Rahman (Housing, Local Government and Rural Development). “The others are Asahan assemblyman Datuk Dr Fairul Nizam Roslan (Tourism, Heritage, Culture and Unity) and Ayer Limau assemblyman Datuk Hameed Mytheen Kunju Basheer (Infrastructure, Transport and Utilities).

items.title: ‘Don’t be petty’: Anthony Loke tells Wee Ka Siong over ECRL launch approval concerns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 19 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke has hit back at MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong over concerns that the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) launch could be held up by the absence of a Transport Minister, telling him not to be petty. Wee had questioned whether the government had secured the necessary approval for the launch, saying the Land Public Transport Act 2010 requires the Transport Minister’s approval before a new railway system can begin operations. Loke, who tendered his resignation as Transport Minister on November 10, said the Prime Minister could assume responsibility for a ministry without a minister or appoint another Cabinet member to temporarily carry out its duties.

items.title: Setia Alam landslide: Road near Sri Pinang Apartments closed, no casualties
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 19 — A landslide on the hillside near the Sri Pinang Apartments on Persiaran Setia Makmur, Setia Alam, here today was reported to not involve any casualties. Meanwhile, the Shah Alam City Council (MBSA) announced through a post on the Threads application that the road in that area has been temporarily closed for safety reasons. The post said that safety ropes and barriers have been installed around the affected area to prevent road users from entering the risk zone.

items.title: No protection for chicken abattoirs flouting halal rules, Selangor says
items.summary: State Islamic Affairs and Innovation Culture Committee chairman Dr Mohammad Fahmi Ngah said the move was intended to respect the investigation process and subsequent legal proceedings involving 11 unlicensed chicken slaughtering and processing premises in the state. He said the identities of those involved should only be disclosed once the cases went to court to avoid embarrassing individuals or triggering legal implications. Mohammad Fahmi said the 11 premises without certified slaughterers comprised one case in Puchong, five premises previously subjected to enforcement action and another five newly identified through a recent review of local authorities’ inventories.

items.title: Perak police rule out foul play in death of Form Three student at Kuala Kangsar boarding school
items.summary: IPOH, Nov 19 — The Form Three student found dead at a boarding school in Kuala Kangsar yesterday died from neck constriction, police said. Perak Police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the cause of death was established following a post-mortem examination conducted at the Forensic Medicine Department of Taiping Hospital today. He said investigations found no evidence of foul play or bullying in connection with the student’s death.

items.title: Police hunt four gang members after robbery mastermind killed in Ipoh shootout
items.summary: IPOH, Nov 19 — Police have launched an intensive manhunt for four fugitives after the alleged mastermind of a violent interstate robbery syndicate was shot dead in a gun battle with detectives in Ipoh early today. The deceased suspect, a 39-year-old Malaysian carrying 17 prior criminal records, was killed along Jalan Persiaran Lembah Perpaduan around 2.30am after opening fire on a joint surveillance team comprising Bukit Aman and Perak Criminal Investigation Department (CID) personnel. Addressing a press conference at the Perak police headquarters today, Bukit Aman CID director Datuk M. Kumar detailed how the tactical intercept unfolded.

items.title: Malaysian govt weighs changes to drug law to shift focus from punishment to rehabilitation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR، Nov 19 — The government is willing to consider a review of Section 15(1) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 as part of efforts to enhance drug treatment and rehabilitation، as drug-related offences account for nearly half of all convicted prisoners in the country. In view of this، the government has noted the suggestion to review Section 15(1) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952. He said that between January and September this year، 12,255 prisoners were serving sentences for taking drugs under Section 15(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952، while another 31,827 were serving sentences for possessing small amounts of drugs.

items.title: From green spaces to elder care, Hannah Yeoh outlines what makes a prosperous KL
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR، Nov 19 — Wealth should not just be accumulated but also enjoyed and shared with others، Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said today. Speaking at the official opening of HSBC Wealth Centre here today، Yeoh said the government’s priority was to strengthen the Malaysian economy to ensure that prosperity could be enjoyed by all، stressing that economic growth remained fundamental to the country’s progress. She said Kuala Lumpur was also focusing on creating a liveable urban environment for people to enjoy their wealth and quality of life، including protecting green spaces، reducing flash flood risks، improving connectivity and preserving the city’s heritage.

items.title: Pontian fire damages 100m of conveyor belts linking jetty to coal storage
items.summary: PONTIAN, Nov 19 — A midday fire damaged three industrial rubber conveyor belts connecting the marine jetty to the coal storage facility at the Tanjung Bin Energy power complex in Kukup today. “Following the call, 13 personnel supported by a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT), a Compact Fire Rescue Tender (CFRT), and a Hilux four-wheel-drive vehicle were immediately dispatched to the scene. “Upon arrival, the team discovered a fire had damaged three rubber conveyor belts, spanning approximately 100 metres, which connect the jetty to the Malakoff Tanjung Bin coal storage facility.

items.title: Home minister: Malaysia, China step up cooperation against cross-border crime, cyber fraud
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR، Nov 19 — Malaysia and China will continue to strengthen bilateral cooperation in security and law enforcement، particularly in addressing increasingly complex cross-border crime threats. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the commitment was reaffirmed during his meeting with China’s State Councilor and Minister of Public Security Wang Xiaohong in Shenzhen، China، yesterday. Saifuddin Nasution said the historic meeting also saw the signing of relevant cooperation documents as part of the ongoing commitment between the two countries.

items.title: Fahmi: Malaysia to test emergency alert system near Parliament on Nov 23, nationwide on Nov 29
items.summary: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) would issue public service announcements (PSAs) to inform the public about the alert messages and sounds they would receive on their mobile phones. He said the simulation test was aimed at ensuring that people understood the notifications were part of a system test and not actual emergency alerts. Fahmi said users would not need to download or install any applications، as the system would send alerts directly to compatible mobile phones.

items.title: Police link man killed in Chow Kit shootout to string of armed robberies
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 19 — The man who was shot dead in an exchange of gunfire with police in Chow Kit here early yesterday is believed to have been involved in a series of robberies since early May and linked to nine separate cases. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the nine cases were identified after the victims recognised the suspect, helping investigators establish his alleged involvement in the crimes. “Kuala Lumpur police are confident that we will be able to uncover the network and identify individuals who conspired with the main suspect,” he told a press conference following a case exhibits disposal ceremony organised by the Kuala Lumpur Police Contingent Headquarters’ Criminal Investigation Department at the Alam Damai Police Post here today.

items.title: ‘All I want is a transparent probe’: Father breaks silence on son’s death in Perak school
items.summary: TAIPING, Nov 19 — The father of a Form Three student who was found dead at a school in Perak has called for a transparent and thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding his son’s death. Mohd Idzwan Razali, 48, said he was remaining calm and leaving it to the authorities to determine the actual cause of the incident. Mohd Idzwan, who is self-employed, said he was informed of the incident involving his third child of five by the police and the school principal yesterday evening.

items.title: Johor Baru police probe viral video of boy hit by car near school
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU، Nov 19 — Police have initiated investigations into a social media video where a young boy was injured after being hit by a car in front of a school in Bandar Baru Uda here yesterday. Johor Bahru North police chief Assistant Commissioner Azrol Anuar Nor said that authorities were alerted of the 12-second video that was uploaded on the Threads platform. Azrol Anuar said the injured boy was rushed to the Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) for medical treatment.

items.title: ‘See you tomorrow’: Negeri Sembilan MB Ismail Lasim keeps reporters guessing amid resignation uncertainty
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR، Nov 19 — Negeri Sembilan Mentri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has left reporters guessing about his political future after repeatedly telling them to meet him the following day when questioned about his position amid uncertainty over his resignation. Asked whether he was scheduled to have an audience with Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir tomorrow، Ismail laughed before once again telling reporters: “Jumpa esok” (See you tomorrow). Zambry said coalition chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi، who is also Umno president، had received a copy of Ismail’s resignation letter dated November 16 and addressed to Tuanku Muhriz.

items.title: Update your phones to receive Malaysia’s new emergency alerts, MCMC tells public
items.summary: CYBERJAYA، Nov 19 — Malaysians have been urged to update their mobile phone operating systems to ensure their devices can receive emergency notifications under the country’s new Early Warning System (EWS)، which is being rolled out in stages. The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) said the system uses Cell Broadcast System (CBS) technology to send alerts simultaneously to compatible mobile phones within designated geographical areas، without requiring users to download an application، register or subscribe to a dedicated service. As an initial guide، devices expected to support EWS alerts include Apple iPhone 11 and newer models running iOS 27.2 or later، Android phones operating on Android 12 or later، and Huawei devices using EMUI 16 or later، subject to final technical confirmation.

items.title: Selangor records 439 TNB cable theft cases since 2023, losses hit RM62.7m
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 19 — A total of 439 cable theft cases involving Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) assets were recorded in Selangor from Jan 1, 2023 to Sept 30 this year, resulting in losses amounting to RM62.7 million. Meanwhile, Izham said the Selangor Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) recorded 38 cases of cable and equipment theft at pump houses and water gates between 2023 and 2026, involving losses estimated at RM1.5 million. “Klang district recorded the highest losses at RM667,000 involving eight cases, followed by Kuala Langat (17 cases, RM499,000), Kuala Selangor (10 cases, RM318,000) and Sepang (three cases, RM47,000),” he said during the State Legislative Assembly sitting today.

items.title: Home Ministry purges 36 errant Immigration staff linked to pass scam
items.summary: Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Dr Shamsul Anuar Nasarah said the Home Ministry (KDN) would not compromise on matters involving integrity, adding that several special operations had been conducted in collaboration with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to address internal misconduct and corruption. He said the digitalisation of the PLKS through the full implementation of the electronic Temporary Employment Visit Pass (ePLKS) system, which eliminates the need for physical stickers, had also helped curb the forgery of employment-related documents. Earlier, in response to an original question from Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (MUDA-Muar) on the breakdown of undocumented foreign nationals and enforcement efforts, Shamsul Anuar said JIM had arrested 35,109 foreign nationals during enforcement operations between Jan 1 and Sept 15 this year.

items.title: WhatsApp group misunderstanding sparked Johor school assault initially suspected to be bullying, say police
items.summary: TANGKAK, Nov 19 — A misunderstanding in a WhatsApp group is believed to have triggered the assault of a 14-year-old boy by three older students at a secondary school in Johor on November 13, police said today. Tangkak police chief Superintendent Roslan Mohd Talib said police were alerted to the incident after a report was lodged the following day. Roslan said police subsequently identified and detained three 15-year-old boys to assist with the investigation.

items.title: BN lawmakers call for internal audit, police probe over leaked Najib pardon papers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 19 — Several Barisan Nasional federal lawmakers today urged the public “to lodge as many police reports as possible”, as they called on the authorities to investigate who leaked the Federal Territories Pardons Board minutes that discussed Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s conditional pardon. The members of parliament also called on Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar to conduct an internal audit to snuff out the parties they claimed had violated the Official Secrets Act. “Second, urging the Chief Secretary to the Government (KSN) to conduct an immediate security audit and internal investigation to identify the mastermind behind this leak of confidential government information,” the MPs added.

items.title: Onn Hafiz thanks Anwar for RM4.86b federal allocation for Johor projects
items.summary: Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the allocation would help realise Johor’s development aspirations on a larger scale. He said the allocation involves a total of 94 new projects and 515 continuation projects in the state. He said this while presenting the Johor Budget 2027 at the Johor State Assembly (DUN) session at the Sultan Ismail Building, Kota Iskandar here.
